item.text: The largest maintainability issue so far is duplicated species behavior plus hard-coded population setup. I’m checking the species hierarchy next so I can extract shared logic without changing simulation rules unnecessarily.

There are clear extraction points: repeated breeding-partner scans, repeated movement/act sequencing in species classes, and repeated “clear after eaten” code. I’m reading the concrete species now to make the smallest useful refactor.
The concrete predator and prey classes mostly differ by constants and their inactive time window. I’m checking the remaining species and the field API before extracting common helpers.

I’m going to make a focused structural refactor rather than a broad rewrite: centralize shared animal lifecycle, breeding checks, plant-eating behavior, and population rules while preserving the existing class model and public constructors.

I’ve found a conservative path that removes duplicated behavior without changing the flat source layout or requiring a build tool. The main edits are in `Animal`, `Predator`, `Prey`, concrete species, and `Populator`.
I added shared animal helpers for mate detection, disease checks, target selection, and movement/removal. Next I’m moving the repeated predator and prey step logic into their abstract base classes.
Predators now share a single lifecycle implementation while each predator class still owns its constants and inactive time. I’m applying the same pattern to prey, including shared plant-food lookup.
With the base behavior in place, I’m trimming concrete species down to their configuration and factory methods. This is where most of the duplicate code disappears.
The predator classes are now reduced to constants plus a one-line `act` method. I’m doing the same for the herbivore classes and letting `Prey` own plant lookup and ordinary movement.
Vulture has the same duplicated mate check pattern, so I’m moving that into `Scavenger` as well and reusing the shared animal disease/move helpers there.
I’m also centralizing the “remove consumed item from the field but keep its simulation object state” operation, which was duplicated in prey and plant classes.

The last structural hotspot is `Populator`: the species probabilities, colors, and factories are spread across a long conditional chain. I’m replacing that with ordered population rules so adding a species becomes a one-entry change.
The main refactor edits are in place. I’m compiling now to catch type errors from the hierarchy changes and any stale imports.
